en: Susiddhikara Sūtra on the Method of Offerings, Volume One.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha of Central India during the Great Tang Dynasty.
I take refuge in all the Tathāgatas, as well as the Dharma and the assembly of Bodhisattvas.
The Lotus Vajra Family, together with all its retinues—
I now explain the methods of offering and recitation according to the teachings,
omitting the common elements shared by the three families, as well as their sequential order and correspondences.
First, one observes the location of the divine chamber, and further clarifies its ritual procedures;
one receives the mantras face-to-face, as well as the methods for forming hand-seals (mudrā);
and regarding the entrances and exits outside, the method for dividing and purifying the earth.
The method for sweeping and cleaning the shrine chamber; The method for removing withered flowers and the like;
The method for bathing and performing self-consecration; The method for offering three handfuls of water;
The method for going to the door of the shrine chamber, changing garments, and sprinkling the body.
Upon entering the chamber, one should perform prostrations; the ritual for preparing various offering implements;
the methods for the rosary and the divine cord; the methods for the *kuśa* grass ring and so forth;
the offering of *argha* water; and the ritual for arranging the precious throne.
Furthermore, he reveals the samaya: the method for removing bodily obstacles and difficulties;
the methods for expulsion and purging impurities, as well as for attaining purity and luster;
and the methods for protecting the body, establishing the boundary, and [securing] the eight directions, above, and below.
First, one should visualize the deity’s seat and contemplate the dharma of the Honored One;
in whatever direction or place one may be, one should invoke the Honored Dharma.
Having invoked the Honored One with their respective root mantras, one should offer the supplication.
Immediately dispel [obstacles] from the māras; this is the method for offering a seat and requesting them to sit.
Furthermore, demonstrate the *samaya*; this is the method for immediately offering *argha* water, bathing the Honored One, and offering robes.
Next, offer unguents, flowers, incense, food, and drink; perform the rite of offering lamps;
employ the mantras and mudrās; practice the method of mental offering;
perform praises, repentance, and so forth; and protect both the ritual site and oneself.
And protect that location, then perform the rite for binding the great boundary (mahā-sīmā);
prepare the vajra and the methods for the rosary and so forth;
fulfill the section on mantras, and next follow the rite for sitting and recitation.
Request the fulfillment of one's original aspirations, protect the recitations performed,
and dedicate the merit of the Dharma by giving rise to vast and expansive vows;
furthermore, offer argha water, unguents, incense, and other ritual offerings.
Furthermore, one should observe the *samaya*, protect the ritual site and oneself,
and release the boundaries previously established; thereafter, perform the dismissal of the deities,
as well as the *homa* and its auxiliary branches, including the hearth-deity (*kuṇḍadevatā*) and the earth.
The ritual for performing fire offerings;
the method for reciting Vaipulya sutras and constructing caityas;
followed by the practice of meditations such as loving-kindness and the contemplation of the six recollections.
Such sequences as these have now been briefly explained by me.
Regarding "one who sees the location of the divine chamber," this refers to one who enters the maṇḍala, upon which flower falls, and takes refuge in that deity.

Regarding the clarification of the ritual methods: this refers to having received the supreme empowerment of the vidyā-mantra, being authorized by the ācārya, and being permitted to transmit the dharma-empowerment as well as to perform all other empowerments.

Regarding those who receive mantras and mudrās: the recipients of the Dharma shall bathe to become pure, don fresh and clean garments, and, kneeling in the lotus posture at a clean location, reverently face the ācārya to personally receive the mantras and perform the mudrās.
At that time, the ācārya first recites it three times and transmits it to the other.
Having received it, the recipient recites it himself three times, giving rise to profound joy, and receives and upholds it with the highest reverence; this constitutes the mutual reception.
Having made offerings to the ācārya according to one’s capacity and having extensively understood the Dharma, one may then perform this sequence of recitation.
Regarding the external places of entry and exit: once one has risen in the early morning, when going to a defiled place, one should protect the body using the impure wrathful mantra.

The mantra is: *Oṃ kṛtāṅga hūṃ*. As for the mudrā: form a fist with the right hand and extend the thumb straight upward; this protects five locations—namely, the crown of the head, the two shoulders, the heart, the throat, and the nape of the neck. This is the minor heart-mudrā (*hṛdaya-mudrā*); there is also a separate major mudrā (*mahāmudrā*).

Next, regarding the division of earth for cleansing: one should use five portions of earth to cleanse the lower part of the body; three portions to wash the area of the urinary passage; three portions exclusively to wash the left hand; and seven portions to wash both hands together. If one fears it is not yet clean, one may wash as much as necessary, with cleanliness as the limit.
All the aforementioned piles of earth must be consecrated with the *sparśa-mantra* and its mudrā, recited seven times, before being employed.
Next, one should sprinkle oneself with the mantra.
The mantra is as follows:

Recite three times: "Oṃ śrutidhāraṇī hūṃ ha. As for the mudrā: extend the five fingers of the right hand straight with the tips touching; then bend the middle joint of the ring finger so that it aligns with the palm, and turn the thumb and little finger forward.
As for the method of sipping water: squatting in silence, place both hands between the knees; cupping the water with the palms, ensure there are no bubbles and drink it without making a sound.
Having drunk three times, one then uses the hand to moisten water and wipes the lips twice.

At that time, as impurities, mucus, saliva, or phlegm from coughing may touch the tongue between the teeth within the mouth, one again drinks water and wipes the lips as before, once more employing this mudrā and reciting the mantra.

Within that mudrā, first touch the thumbs and ring fingers to the two eyes, then the mouth, the two ears, the nose, the two shoulders, the navel, the heart, and finally touch the throat; thus one accomplishes the protection of the body and the purification of the sense faculties.

Next, regarding the sweeping and cleaning of the shrine room: this means that according to the specific accomplishment and the particular requirements of the rite, one should select a location that is appropriate for it, pleasing to the mind, and free from all obstacles and difficulties.

That ground shall be cleared of thorns, insect nests, pits, hollows, rubble, husks, bones, hair, and ashes such as salt, charcoal, or cinders; the foul earth shall be excavated and replaced with pure soil.
Construct a chamber above, making it firm and airtight so that no wind may enter; open the door facing east, north, or west, or toward the south according to the specific requirements of the rite.

Once the divine chamber has been constructed, smear it with cow dung and sprinkle it with pure water; or, using scented ointment mixed with pure water, one should apply it to the ground while reciting this vidyā-mantra.

"Recite this three times. Should one at any time forget the recitation, err in the ritual procedure, or violate the samaya, one should recite this vidyā-mantra three, seven, or one hundred and eight times each day; this will be able to eliminate those transgressions.
Regarding the removal of withered flowers: after having offered the honored flowers, one first recites this mantra to remove those withered flowers, saying:
"Oṃ kṣate mahākṣate khāne svāhā. Next, the mantra for sweeping the ground is spoken:
"Oṃ hara hara rāhu graha haranaya svāhā. Next, the mantra for smearing the ground is taught: "Oṃ karale mahākarale svāhā. Recite this three times.
One should first sprinkle and sweep the shrine room, remove withered flowers, and purify all the offering vessels; only after that should one go to bathe—thus it is taught.
When going to bathe, one should first protect the ritual implements with this mantra and mudrā, and only then proceed.

The mantra is: "Oṃ śuklavajri āḥ. Recite this three times. As for the form of the hand-mudrā: make a fist with the right hand, extend the thumb straight upward, and join the index and middle fingers together.

Regarding "first performing the samaya": this means that for any ritual procedure, one must first perform the samaya, and only thereafter perform all other matters such as the protection of the body; thus it is taught.
Next, the samaya mantras and mudrās are explained.
First, the mantra of the Buddha Family is as follows:
"Oṃ tathāgataguhyā nābhavāya svāhā. Recite this three times; this is the samaya mantra of the Buddha Family.

As for the characteristics of the mudrā: extend the ten fingers of both hands straight forward with palms facing upward and sides touching; slightly bend the upper joints of the two index fingers—this is the samaya-mudrā.
Next, the *samaya* mantra and mudrā of the Padma family are explained. The mantra is:
"Oṃ padmanābhāya svāhā. This is the *samaya* mantra of the Padma family; both "svā" and "hā" are pronounced with a departing tone (*udātta*).

Regarding the characteristics of this mudrā: first, one should join the palms together; then, the six fingers of both hands should be extended outward so that they do not touch one another, while the thumbs and little fingers of both hands remain joined as before. The hollow space within the joined palms should be like the center of a lotus flower, with the six middle fingers slightly bent. This is the Samaya-mudrā of the Lotus Family.
Next, the *samaya* mantra and mudrā of the Vajra Family are explained. The mantra is: "Oṃ vajranābāya svāhā.

Recite this three times; this is the Vajra-samaya mantra. As for the form of the mudrā: place the right hand over the left, with the backs of both hands joined together. Insert the right thumb through the space between the fingers of the left hand, and place the left thumb against the fingers of the right hand. Slightly separate the six middle fingers of both hands so that they resemble a three-pronged vajra. This is the Vajra-samaya mudrā.
Regarding "binding all obstacles": this means binding all obstacles by means of the *muṇḍarī* hand-seal (*mudrā*) and mantra.

As for the form of the seal: place the left hand upon the upper part of the right forearm; with the thumb, pinch the nail of the little finger, and extend the middle three fingers like a three-pronged vajra.

Again, place the right hand upon the upper part of the left shoulder, using the thumb to press against the nail of the little finger, while extending the middle three fingers like a three-pronged ritual pestle.

Standing facing east, bend the knee of the left leg and lean forward toward the right foot; extend the right foot wide for two chi or more, placing it crosswise upon the ground. Bite down on the lower right lip, glare with angry eyes to the left, and silently visualize yourself as Kuṇḍalī.
Recite its root mantra, which says:
"Namaḥ ratnatrayāya, namaḥ mañjuśriye vajrapāṇaye, mahāyakṣa..."
Saṃpuṭāya namaḥ vajrakrodhāya neṣṭarudrakṣatapañjara-bāhye tadyathā oṃ amṛtakuṇḍali kha kha kha.
KHAKHE KHAKHE KṢARĀJA VIŚPOṬAYA VIŚPOṬAYA SARVAVIÑJANA VINIGRAHAṂ KURU MAHĀJÑĀNAPRATYEKADHĀRAṆĪVIDANTAKARA.
"Recite 'ĀṆAYA HŪṂ PHAṬ' seven times. This is the mantra for binding all calamities.

At the very end of the mantra, upon the word "bandha bandha," one should immediately form fists with three fingers of both hands; the little fingers should remain as they were, unbent. By this, all calamities shall be bound and restrained.
Regarding the method for bathing: first, using mantras and mudrās, take earth and form it into three heaps in order to purify the body.

The mantra is: "Oṃ nikhāna vasudhe svāhā. Recite this five times; this is the mantra for purifying the earth. As for the characteristics of the mudrā: interlace the two hands with the fingers pressing against the backs of the hands. Extend both index fingers upright so they touch each other, and place both thumbs side-by-side upright, leaning against the sides of the index fingers. Cover the taken earth with this mudrā while reciting the mantra five times, and then take it.

Regarding "expelling" (*vidhūnana*): for all actions one undertakes, one must first perform the expulsion; only thereafter should one proceed with any other matters. The teaching is as follows. The mantra for expulsion is:

*Namaḥ samantavajrāṇāṃ hūṃ haṃ taṃ mamatā vidambha svayamkārāya hūṃ phaṭ*. Recite this seven times. This is the mantra for expulsion. As for the mudrā: bend the left thumb into the palm; press the thumb with the middle and ring fingers; bend the index finger so its tip touches the side of the middle joint of the middle finger; likewise bend the little finger so it touches the side of the middle joint of the ring finger. Then extend the arm and rotate it three times clockwise above the head, and seal the five places of the body.

Press the thumb of the right hand against the nail of the little finger, extend the remaining three fingers straight upward to form the shape of a *vajra*, and cross them at the side of the waist; the ritual procedure is as before—this is the mudrā for expelling obstructors.
Furthermore, there are the mantras and hand gestures for expulsion (*vidhūnana*).

The mantra is: "Oṃ vajratāra hūṃ phaṭ. This is the mantra for expulsion. As for the characteristics of the hand gesture: place the fingers of the right hand upon the palm of the left hand; perform this three times. This is the hand gesture for expulsion.
Furthermore, there are the mantras and mudrās for exorcism.

The mantra is: "Oṃ kili kīla kara vāraṇa hūṃ phaṭ. This is the mantra for exorcism. As for the characteristics of the mudrā: snap the fingers three times with both hands; this is the mudrā for exorcism.
Regarding the method for protecting the body: one uses this mantra and mudrā to bind the boundaries of the ten directions and to protect the body. The mantra is: *Oṃ saṃkari samayaṃ svāhā*.

This is the mantra for binding the boundaries and protecting the body. As for the characteristics of the mudrā: with the right hand, press the thumb against the nail of the little finger; keep the remaining three fingers slightly apart and held upright. This is called the Vajra-mudrā. It is used to bind the boundaries above, below, and the eight directions, as well as for self-protection. This is the mudrā for binding the boundaries and protecting the body.

Next, using mantras and mudrās, one should seal one’s own body as well as the water, earth, and cleansing powder (kaṣāya). This shall effect the removal of impurities (*malotsarga*) and purification. The mantra is: *Oṃ kīli vajra hūṃ phaṭ*. Recite this seven times;

this is the mantra for the removal of impurities. As for the form of the mudrā: with the right hand, press the thumb against the nail of the little finger, keep the remaining three fingers slightly spread and held straight up, and cross them at the waist with the three fingers pointing forward. Perform the same mudrā with the left hand. By using these hands to seal and touch all objects, the removal of impurities and purification are accomplished. This is the mudrā for the removal of impurities.
Next, perform purification using the mantra and mudrā of Kuṇḍalī.

The mantra is: "Oṃ amṛte hūṃ phaṭ. Recite this seven times; this is the purification mantra. As for the form of the mudrā: form a fist with the right hand, take water, and recite the mantra seven times. Sprinkle it upon all objects, the hands, and the crown of the head; thus they become purified. This is the purification mudrā.
Next, use mantras and mudrās to produce a lustrous radiance. The mantra is: "Oṃ kili kili vajra hūṃ phaṭ.

Recite this seven times; this is the mantra for producing radiance. As for the characteristics of the mudrā: with the left hand, press the thumb upon the nail of the little finger; keep the remaining three fingers slightly spread and held upright. Extend the arm, and with the right hand, form this same mudrā to support the underside of the left elbow. By stamping all objects touched and one's own body with the right-hand mudrā, they become radiant. This is the mudrā for producing radiance.
Next, stir the water with a mantra and a mudrā. The mantra is: *Oṃ hūṃ haṃ vajra-vajriṇi svāhā*.

There is no limit to the number of recitations; one should simply recite this as many times as possible. This is the mantra for stirring the water. As for the characteristics of the mudrā: cross the two hands outwardly, join the tips of the two thumbs together while holding them upright, and bend the two index fingers slightly so that their nails touch. This is the mudrā for stirring the water.
Next, take earth with a mantra and a mudrā to smear upon the body.

The mantra is: "Oṃ bhu ra ja va ra hūṃ. Recite this seven times; this is the mantra for smearing the earth. As for the form of the mudrā: take earth and mix it with water, rub the two hands together, and then use the right hand to smear it all over the body. This is the mudrā for smearing the body with earth.
Next, one should recite the water-mantra of Kuṇḍalī using the appropriate hand-gesture (mudrā).

The mantra is: "Oṃ amṛte hūṃ phaṭ. Recite this seven times; this is the water-mantra for recitation. As for the characteristics of the hand-gesture: first, extend the right hand flatly, pressing the thumb upon the tips of the middle and ring fingers, slightly bending the index and little fingers. While reciting the mantra, stir the water with this seal and bathe; this is the water-seal for recitation.
Next, one should dispel the obstacles of the *vināyakas* within the body by means of mantras and mudrās.

The mantra is: "Oṃ amṛte hana hana hūṃ phaṭ. This is the mantra for dispelling the *vināyakas* within the body. As for the form of the mudrā: clench both hands into fists by bending the thumbs into the palms; extend the two index fingers and interlace them left and right into the "tiger's mouth" (the space between the thumb and forefinger). Move this mudrā from the crown of the head downward to the feet and release it. This is the mudrā for dispelling the *vināyakas* within the body.
Next, one should protect the five parts of the body with the Mañjuśrī-mañjughoṣa (Muṇḍarī) mantra and mudrā.

The mantra is: "Oṃ vajra jñiṃ praṇipataye svāhā. Recite this five times; this is the protection mantra. As for the form of the mudrā: interlace the two little fingers and insert them into the palms; press the two ring fingers over the crossed little fingers; join the tips of the two middle fingers; slightly bend the two index fingers so they rest against the side of the upper joints of the middle fingers; and extend the two thumbs straight up beside the middle fingers, separated by the distance of a single barley grain. Touch the five places with the seal; when the seal is formed, it protects the body—this is the protection mudrā.
Next, one should consecrate each portion of the earth by reciting the mantra and performing the mudrā.

The mantra is: "Oṃ durbidurgāya durbiprajvalini svāhā. Recite this three times; this is the mantra for consecrating the earth. As for the form of the mudrā: join the tips of the index fingers and little fingers of both hands; bend the two middle fingers and two ring fingers into the palms so that their backs touch; and with the two thumbs, press down on the tips of the middle and ring fingers respectively.

Take one portion from the three heaps of earth previously set out; seal it with the mudrā and recite [the mantra] over it three times. Use this to wash from the feet up to the navel, then wash the hands and sprinkle water for purification.
Repeat this washing and sprinkling for the second and third portions in the same manner.
Again, take another handful and recite as before, using it to wash from the navel up to the neck;
again, take another handful and recite as before, using it to wash from the neck up to the crown of the head.
Having finished, recite the mantra again.

Bathe as you wish, then form this mudrā once more and recite the mantra while rotating it all around the body; release the mudrā at the heart. This is called the Armor Mudrā (Kavaca-mudrā); it is the mudrā for the ground of recitation.
Next, recite the root mantra of Kuntali and stir the water with the hand seal (*mudrā*), then bathe as you wish. The mantra is: *Namaḥ ratnatrayāya maṃśi...*
